Save note content when editor disappears
  Extract persistNote() from saveNote() to allow saving without closing
  the editor. Call persistNote() from onDisappear (when notch retracts)
  and cancelEdit() so user changes are never silently discarded.

Atoll: deliver Spotify Canvas as lockscreen wallpaper without album-art flash

Two fixes for the right-click-artwork-to-wallpaper flow on Spotify
tracks that have a Canvas video.

1. Force AllSpacesAndDisplays.Type and SystemDefault.Type to
   "individual" while the artwork is active (was: keep existing
   value via nil-coalescing). On macOS Tahoe the user-level
   wallpaper rotation honors the parent Type field, so leaving it
   as "folder" caused WallpaperAgent to advance to the next image
   in a rotating wallpaper pack instead of honoring the patched
   single-image / aerial choice. The original Type is preserved in
   the plist backup at temp/atoll_wallpaper_backup.plist and is
   restored byte-for-byte on dismiss, so rotation resumes normally
   after the artwork is dismissed. The forced override is also
   applied to nested Displays / Spaces blocks but only when Type
   was already present, to avoid mutating block shapes that
   intentionally omit it.

2. When the Canvas is expected at right-click time
   (effectiveVideoURL != nil), defer applyArtworkToPlist and
   restartWallpaperAgent entirely. Previously the flow applied raw
   album art as the static wallpaper, restarted the agent, then
   prepared and applied the aerial in a second restart, causing a
   visible flash of the raw album cover. The deferred path stores
   the blurred fallback URL in pendingFallbackStaticURL and only
   touches the plist once: with the aerial on success, or with the
   blurred album cover via applyDeferredStaticFallback if the
   aerial asset prep or aerial-plist patch fails. The in-app
   videoWindow continues to mask the desktop wallpaper during prep
   on the unlocked screen; the lock screen simply transitions from
   the existing wallpaper straight to the Canvas video.

The earlier ?? nil-coalescing in patchWallpaperEntries also covered
per-Display, per-Space.Default, and per-Space.Displays Type fields,
so those are forced too where present.

Signed-off-by: Jis G Jacob <studiokeys@blissroms.org>

normal Xcode-attached development. The restart-alert dialog firing
mid-development is disruptive and not actionable.

developers running under Xcode aren't interrupted by spurious
restart prompts. The poll interval, cooldown, and alert text all

Fix focus modes always showing Do Not Disturb on non-English macOS

When macOS reports a focus mode with a localized name (e.g. "Travail" for
Work in French) but without a specific bundle identifier, resolve() failed
to match the foreign name against its English-only lookup table and fell
back to returning .doNotDisturb. This caused the wrong identifier
("com.apple.donotdisturb.mode") to be stored, making every focus mode
render as Do Not Disturb regardless of which mode was actually active.

Fix by treating an unrecognized name with no identifier as .custom instead

- Artwork is cached per track to avoid redundant network requests
- Simplified the AppleScript by removing the ineffective Library playlist lookup fallback and collapsed the duplicate macOS 26 / pre-26 script branches
- Replaced `JSONSerialization` dictionary access with `Decodable` structs (`ITunesSearchResponse`, `ITunesTrack`) to match codebase conventions

Atoll: deliver Spotify Canvas as lockscreen wallpaper without album-art flash

Two fixes for the right-click-artwork-to-wallpaper flow on Spotify
tracks that have a Canvas video.

1. Force AllSpacesAndDisplays.Type and SystemDefault.Type to
   "individual" while the artwork is active (was: keep existing
   value via nil-coalescing). On macOS Tahoe the user-level
   wallpaper rotation honors the parent Type field, so leaving it
   as "folder" caused WallpaperAgent to advance to the next image
   in a rotating wallpaper pack instead of honoring the patched
   single-image / aerial choice. The original Type is preserved in
   the plist backup at temp/atoll_wallpaper_backup.plist and is
   restored byte-for-byte on dismiss, so rotation resumes normally
   after the artwork is dismissed. The forced override is also
   applied to nested Displays / Spaces blocks but only when Type
   was already present, to avoid mutating block shapes that
   intentionally omit it.

2. When the Canvas is expected at right-click time
   (effectiveVideoURL != nil), defer applyArtworkToPlist and
   restartWallpaperAgent entirely. Previously the flow applied raw
   album art as the static wallpaper, restarted the agent, then
   prepared and applied the aerial in a second restart, causing a
   visible flash of the raw album cover. The deferred path stores
   the blurred fallback URL in pendingFallbackStaticURL and only
   touches the plist once: with the aerial on success, or with the
   blurred album cover via applyDeferredStaticFallback if the
   aerial asset prep or aerial-plist patch fails. The in-app
   videoWindow continues to mask the desktop wallpaper during prep
   on the unlocked screen; the lock screen simply transitions from
   the existing wallpaper straight to the Canvas video.

The earlier ?? nil-coalescing in patchWallpaperEntries also covered
per-Display, per-Space.Default, and per-Space.Displays Type fields,
so those are forced too where present.

Signed-off-by: Jis G Jacob <studiokeys@blissroms.org>

Atoll: raise MemoryUsageMonitor threshold to 4 GiB in DEBUG builds

The 1 GiB resident-size threshold is reasonable for a release build,
but Swift/SwiftUI debug builds plus the AVPlayer-backed Canvas video
pipeline and SkyLight overlay windows can easily exceed it during
normal Xcode-attached development. The restart-alert dialog firing
mid-development is disruptive and not actionable.

Keep the 1 GiB safety net on release, raise to 4 GiB in DEBUG so
developers running under Xcode aren't interrupted by spurious
restart prompts. The poll interval, cooldown, and alert text all
stay the same.

Signed-off-by: Jis G Jacob <studiokeys@blissroms.org>

Atoll: distinguish charging-on-hold from fully charged on lockscreen widget

The lockscreen battery widget treated any plugged-in-but-not-charging
state as 'Fully charged'. macOS pauses charging for battery health
(e.g., optimized battery charging at 80%), so this misreported the
actual battery state.

Now 'Fully charged' shows only at 100% + plugged in; otherwise the
detail label reads '<level>% • On hold' (with a matching accessibility
string). Charging-in-progress and fully-charged states are unchanged.

Atoll: re-SIGSTOP OSDUIHelper across launchd respawns

OSDUIHelper jetsam-exits when idle and launchd spawns a fresh PID on
the next media-key press, so the one-shot SIGSTOP only suppressed the
first incarnation. SystemOSDManager now polls for the PID after
kickstart and runs a background watcher that re-SIGSTOPs every new
incarnation, with state guarded by OSAllocatedUnfairLock. Watcher is
torn down on enableSystemHUD().

Fixes the legacy OSDUIHelper duplicate-HUD path in #419.

The macOS 26 Liquid Glass HUD (loginwindow -> BezelServices ->
ControlCenter SystemBannerService) is a separate render path gated by
the com.apple.private.system-banner-client entitlement and is not
suppressible from a regular user-space app; it needs a privileged
SMAppService helper and is out of scope here.

Fix brightness HUD not working on macOS Tahoe 26.5

The brightness HUD broke on Tahoe because Apple deprecated/changed the
DisplayServices private framework and stopped posting the BezelEngine
distributed notifications that Atoll relied on for change detection.

This commit:
- Adds CoreBrightnessDisplayClient using Apple's CoreBrightness framework
  (mirrors the existing KeyboardBrightnessClient pattern) as the primary
  brightness read/write path
- Falls back gracefully to DisplayServices then IODisplay if CoreBrightness
  is unavailable
- Adds a lightweight polling fallback (150ms) so the HUD fires even when

Fix focus modes always showing Do Not Disturb on non-English macOS

When macOS reports a focus mode with a localized name (e.g. "Travail" for
Work in French) but without a specific bundle identifier, resolve() failed
to match the foreign name against its English-only lookup table and fell
back to returning .doNotDisturb. This caused the wrong identifier
("com.apple.donotdisturb.mode") to be stored, making every focus mode
render as Do Not Disturb regardless of which mode was actually active.

Fix by treating an unrecognized name with no identifier as .custom instead
of .doNotDisturb, and preserving the provided display name when it is not
an icon slug (slugs contain a dot, display names do not).

ensuring auto-scroll targets only timed events and all-day items remain

Refactor: extract shared auto-scroll helpers, fix scroll target for past/future dates

Address CodeRabbit review comments on PR #566:

1. Extract partitionEvents(), scrollTargetForTimedEvents(), and
   scrollReferenceTime() as free functions — both EventListView and
   StandaloneEventCardList now call the shared implementation,
   eliminating duplication and preventing drift (the Task @MainActor
   deferral was already inconsistent between the two copies).

2. Use selectedDate as reference time instead of Date() when
   determining the scroll target. For today, Date() is used so the
   view scrolls to the current/next event. For past or future days,
   startOfDay is used so the view scrolls to the first event of that
   day rather than jumping to an unexpected position.

3. StandaloneEventCardList.scrollToRelevantEvent now uses
   Task { @MainActor } deferral like EventListView, ensuring
   proxy.scrollTo doesn't no-op when called from onAppear before
   layout is complete.

fix: resume OSDUIHelper synchronously on quit

enableSystemHUD() restores OSDUIHelper on a detached background Task, which
never completes when the app is already terminating. If Atoll was suppressing
the native OSD, OSDUIHelper is left SIGSTOP-frozen after quit, breaking every
native OSD Atoll does not replace (keyboard backlight, external-display
brightness) and leaving a stuck HUD on screen.

Add resumeOSDUIHelperForTermination(), which stops the suppression watcher and
sends SIGCONT inline (blocking until it lands), and call it from
applicationWillTerminate so the helper is always resumed before Atoll exits.

Fix: keep all-day section at fixed single-row height in Dynamic Island panel (#566 follow-up)

The previous design stacked one full row per all-day event in a pinned top
section. In the height-constrained Dynamic Island calendar panel (capped at a
fixed height), two all-day events could consume the entire panel, leaving no
room for the timed-events scroll area — so other time-based events became
invisible and the view could not scroll.

Replace the growing pinned section with a single-row horizontal chip strip
that holds all all-day events and scrolls horizontally when overflowing.
This keeps the all-day section at a constant height regardless of count, so
the timed-events scroll area always retains its full height.

Fix: retrigger auto-scroll when timed events load after view appears (#566)

CodeRabbit flagged that the auto-scroll only fired from .onAppear and
onChange(of: selectedDate). When timedEvents become available asynchronously
after the view appeared, the initial scroll could be missed and the view
stayed at the top.

Add a one-shot trigger on timedEvents becoming non-empty (guarded by a
@State flag) so the initial auto-scroll still fires once, without
re-scrolling on every later data refresh. Applied to both EventListView
(Dynamic Island panel) and StandaloneEventCardList (standalone calendar).

Only DynamicIslandCalendar.swift changed.

Fix: render all-day events as a compact strip in the standalone calendar too (#566)

The standalone calendar window (StandaloneEventCardList) still stacked one
full-height card per all-day event, so two all-day events consumed the whole
panel. Reuse the same AllDayEventsStrip (single fixed-height row of small
chips, like macOS Calendar's Day view) used by the Dynamic Island panel, so
the layout is consistent and multiple all-day events never fill the page.

Only DynamicIslandCalendar.swift changed.

Fix crash when Apple Notes sync encounters duplicate remote note IDs

AppleNotesSyncManager.merge() builds `remoteById` with
Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:). When fetchRemoteNotes() returns two
notes sharing the same id — which Apple Notes can produce across
accounts or on repeated fetches — Swift traps with a fatal _MergeError
("Duplicate values for key"), crashing the whole app on the main thread.

Crashing stack:
  _assertionFailure
  _NativeDictionary.merge(_:isUnique:uniquingKeysWith:)
  Dictionary.init(uniqueKeysWithValues:)
  AppleNotesSyncManager.merge(localNotes:remoteNotes:)  (line 128)
  AppleNotesSyncManager.sync(localNotes:)
  NotchNotesView.syncWithAppleNotes()

Switch to Dictionary(_:uniquingKeysWith:), keeping the entry with the
newer modificationDate on conflict. This tolerates duplicate ids instead
of trapping; downstream logic already keys by id so the surviving entry
is the correct one to retain.

fix(audio): stop Spotify process-tap from hijacking AirPods media control

When the real-time waveform visualizer is on, AudioTap process-taps Spotify
into a private aggregate device. On a Bluetooth output route (e.g. AirPods)
this disturbs the system Now Playing / AVRCP session, so the AirPods pause
gesture finds no target and macOS falls back to Siri instead of pausing.

Only Spotify is affected: it is controlled via AppleScript and registers
weakly with MediaRemote, unlike Apple Music which stays registered.

Skip tapping Spotify while a Bluetooth route is active (visualizer stays live
for Spotify on wired/built-in output and for every other app on any output),
and rebuild the tap on audio-route changes so Spotify is re-included or
excluded when AirPods connect/disconnect.

- AudioRouteManager: add isDefaultOutputBluetooth() querying CoreAudio directly
- AudioTap: skip Spotify PID while Bluetooth output is active
- DynamicIslandApp: restart capture on .systemAudioRouteDidChange

  that was already in flight. The restart also re-reads

- setupAudioTapMusicObservers() is idempotent: the block-based observers
  are retained as tokens and removed before re-registering, so flipping

Show Claude subscription plan badge in the usage card

Read the current user's own subscription tier string from the plaintext
oauthAccount fields in ~/.claude.json (organizationRateLimitTier, falling
back to organizationType) and render it as a small capsule badge next to
the Claude card title. This is best-effort and optional: only the tier
string is read (no credentials/tokens), and if the file is missing or
malformed readPlanLabel() returns nil so no badge shows and the snapshot
is unaffected. The plan field is Claude-only; other providers leave it
nil and are not touched.

Recover Claude quota fetch after OAuth token rotation

ClaudeCredentialStore cached the OAuth credentials on first read and never
re-read the source, so when Claude Code rotated the token (revoking the old
access token, or consuming the refresh token we still held) the usage API
started returning 401 and the quota gauges fell back to "quota unavailable"
until the app was restarted.

Distinguish auth failures (401/403, or a refresh that no longer works) from
other failures, and on an auth failure invalidate the cached credentials,
re-read from source (file -> Keychain, which Claude Code has updated), and
retry the usage request exactly once. Non-auth failures (network/5xx/decode)
do not retry, since reloading credentials would not help. The retry is
bounded to one attempt, the actor keeps credential access serialized, and no
tokens are logged.

Normalize Claude model IDs for pricing; show explicit unavailable estimate

Addresses #664 (part 1: Claude cost/pricing).

Cost was matched by exact model id against the pricing table, but Claude Code
logs native Anthropic ids (claude-opus-4-8, claude-sonnet-5,
claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, sometimes a provider-prefixed
anthropic/claude-4.8-opus-20260528) while the table is keyed OpenRouter-style
(anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet). Every miss set hasUnpricedModel and left the
total at 0, so a card with millions of tokens showed a misleading US/bin/zsh.00+.

getPricing now tries a small ladder of normalized candidate keys before giving
up: it strips the provider prefix and any trailing date stamp, treats dotted
minor versions the same as dashed, and emits both family-first and version-first
word orders (OpenRouter's own Claude naming uses both), each with and without the
anthropic/ prefix. This does not touch pricing.json — that file is maintained
by an external bot, and normalization lives entirely in code. Placeholder rows
whose rates are blank/zero are skipped so they don't report a false $0.00.

When a model genuinely has no table entry the cost stays unpriced, and the card
now shows an explicit "est. n/a" (or "$X.XX+" when a partial amount is known)
instead of a misleading "$0.00+", with a tooltip clarifying the figure is an
API-equivalent estimate from local token counts, not a subscription bill.

Scope note: the fix stays out of JSONLUsageParser.swift, so it does not overlap
the Codex Today/Week counting fix (#664 part 2).

fix(clipboard): widen drag auto-close safety window to 15s

SwiftUI `.onDrag` has no drag-end callback, so the notch is held open by a
bounded safety reset. 4s could expire during a slow drag and let the notch
close mid-drag; widen it to 15s to cover realistic drag durations. A true
completion callback would need an AppKit NSDraggingSource (out of scope here).

fix(llm-usage): follow Claude Code's hash-suffixed Keychain item for quota

Recent Claude Code versions store the OAuth token under a per-install
hash-suffixed Keychain service (`Claude Code-credentials-<hash>`, the hash being
SHA256(CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR)) and no longer update the un-suffixed
`Claude Code-credentials` item. The quota reader hardcoded the un-suffixed name,
so it read a stale/expired token and the Claude card showed "quota unavailable".

Enumerate `Claude Code-credentials*` items by attributes only (no secret access,
so no Keychain prompt) and read the secret of the most-recently-modified one. The
app is a GUI process and cannot see the shell's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so following
the freshest item is what tracks the active config directory. Orthogonal to the
token-refresh path (#685); only the credential source changes.

fix(shelf): remove semaphore deadlocks that stalled every drop

`ShelfItem` is a `@MainActor struct`, and `resolvedContextSync` bridged to its
async sibling with `Task.detached` + `DispatchSemaphore.wait`. Called from the
main actor that is a guaranteed deadlock: the detached task has to hop onto the
main actor, which the semaphore is already blocking. Every call burned its full
5s timeout and returned nil.

`identityKey` sits on that path, and `ShelfStateViewModel.add()` calls it once
per existing *and* per new item while deduplicating, so a single drop froze the
UI for (existing + new) x 5s. `remove()` hit the same wall via
`cleanupStoredData`.

`Bookmark.resolve()` was already nonisolated and synchronous, so the bridge was
never needed. Drop the sync/async context pair entirely and route callers
through a new `resolvedFileURL`.

To keep even that resolve off the main actor, record the path at drop time in
`ShelfItem.cachedPath` (Optional, so old items.json payloads still decode) and
backfill pre-existing items off-actor at launch. `Bookmark.resolveWithoutMounting()`
caps the remaining sync paths so an unreachable network share can't stall the UI.

Also fixes `fileURL`/`URL`, which returned hard-coded nil for file items and
silently emptied 13 call sites — Open, Open With, Show in Finder, Quick Look,
Compress, Copy Path and the image actions were all missing from the context menu.

feat(shelf): add marquee selection model and rubber-band view

Groundwork for dragging a selection rectangle over the shelf.

`ShelfItemHitRegistry` maps item IDs to the live cell `NSView`s. Walking the
view hierarchy isn't possible — the cell view is nested inside a `private` type
in ShelfItemView.swift — and reading frames off AppKit directly means scroll
offset and clipping come out right without mirroring SwiftUI layout through
preferences.

`ShelfSelectionModel` gains a marquee API with its own `isMarqueeSelecting`
flag, deliberately separate from `isDragging`: the latter means "an
NSDraggingSession is carrying items out" and gates `ShelfView.handleDrop`, so
conflating them would make drops silently fail while the band is up.
`reconcileSelection` now also prunes the marquee base set, otherwise an item
removed mid-drag would be resurrected by the next update.

`ShelfMarqueeSelectionView` is plain AppKit rather than a SwiftUI DragGesture:
the cells are covered by `DraggableClickView`, a real NSView that swallows mouse
events, where a SwiftUI gesture would never fire. Drawing the band in `draw(_:)`
also avoids republishing SwiftUI state on every mouse-moved event. Includes
edge auto-scroll (the shelf is a single horizontal row, so the band routinely
needs to reach items scrolled out of view) and Cmd+A / Delete / Escape.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(shelf): drag files out as real file URLs, not plain text

`createPasteboardItem` waited 5s on a semaphore that always deadlocked (see the
earlier commit), then fell through to writing `item.displayName` as plain text.
That is why dropping onto Finder or Mail produced text instead of the file.

Hand AppKit the `NSURL` instead of hand-rolling an `NSPasteboardItem`: it
declares `public.file-url`, `public.url`, `public.url-name` and the legacy
filenames binding in one go, which is what Finder, Mail attachments and Slack
uploads actually look for. An item whose URL can't be resolved is now dropped
from the drag rather than degraded to text.

Second, independent cause of broken drag-out: dragging out necessarily takes the
cursor off the notch, so the hover-exit timer closed the panel mid-drag and tore
down the NSView acting as the drag source. Gate auto-close on `isDragging`, and
re-evaluate hover once the session ends.

Dragging out also offered `.move` to external apps. AppKit has no way to say
"move is allowed but prefer copy" — the destination decides — and Finder moves
by default when the target is on the same volume, silently relocating the user's
original. Copy is now the default, with moving behind a new `allowMoveOnDrag`
setting.

Drops the security-scope calls on the drag path: since the macOS 26 fix,
`Bookmark` produces plain bookmarks, so `startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()`
always returned false and the paired teardown loop never had anything to do.

feat(shelf): wire marquee selection into the shelf panel

Mounts the rubber-band view as an overlay on the ScrollView's content — inside
the document view, above the cells — rather than at the bottom of the panel's
ZStack. Underneath, a mouseDown in the gap right of the last item would go to
the NSScrollView and travel *up* the responder chain, never reaching a sibling

fix(bluetooth): stop the device scan re-entering BluetoothAudioManager's own init

Atoll could trap on launch with
`BUG IN CLIENT OF LIBDISPATCH: trying to lock recursively`, but only while a
Bluetooth audio device was connected — which is why it looked intermittent.

The chain, from the crash report:

    applicationDidFinishLaunching
      LockScreenWeatherManager.shared            (once #1)
        observeAccessoryChanges()
          BluetoothAudioManager.shared           (once #2 begins)
            checkInitialDevices()
              refreshBatteryLevelsForConnectedDevices()
                collectSystemProfilerBatteryLevels()
                  systemProfilerBluetoothDictionary()
                    Process.waitUntilExit()  ->  __CFRunLoopRun
                      SwiftUI NSRunLoop.flushObservers
                        ContentView.body -> NotchLayout()
                          InlineHUD default argument 18
                            BluetoothAudioManager.shared   (once #2 AGAIN) -> trap

`Process.waitUntilExit()` on the main thread runs the run loop while it waits.
That hands control to SwiftUI's run-loop observer mid-initialiser, and the body
it evaluates reads `BluetoothAudioManager.shared` because that is a default
argument of `InlineHUD.init` — re-entering the `swift_once` that is still
constructing the instance. A connected audio device is what makes the
`system_profiler` call slow enough for the observer to get a turn.

Deferring the scan to the next main-queue turn lets `shared` finish publishing
first, so the re-entry is impossible by construction. Observer registration and
the 30-second watchdog timer stay in the initialiser; neither spins the run
loop.

Verified against the branch where it reproduced deterministically (4 of 4 runs
trapped before, 112 of 112 tests pass after, twice, with the same Bluetooth
headset still connected).

Worth a separate look: `Process.waitUntilExit()` is called on the main thread in
three places in this file. Deferring the scan removes the re-entrancy, but those
calls still block the main thread while shelling out.

fix(extensions): the RPC port was open to the local network

`ExtensionRPCServer` is documented as listening on localhost, and it was not:
`NWListener(using:on:)` binds the wildcard address, and nothing checked where
a connection came from. Measured on this Mac before the change:

    Atoll  36966  4u  IPv6  TCP *:9020 (LISTEN)
    $ nc -z 192.168.1.105 9020 → succeeded

So any machine on the same Wi-Fi could open the extension API — where a client
declares who it is by putting a `bundleIdentifier` in the request — and drive
the shelf, live activities, lock-screen widgets and notch experiences.

Now bound to the loopback address of each family. Two listeners rather than
one because a socket bound to 127.0.0.1 does not accept ::1 and vice versa,
and a client resolving "localhost" may arrive on either; each is optional, so
a Mac with one family disabled still serves on the other. Every accepted
connection's peer is checked as well — a bind is one line away from being
widened by accident, and the check costs nothing.

Two details worth keeping:

`requiredLocalEndpoint` and `on: port` may not both be given. Passing both
throws EINVAL at init, which is how the first attempt at this fix managed to
bind nothing at all: the listener silently never started, because the error
path logs at a level that is off by default.

A restarted listener no longer tears down live client connections. A listener
failing says nothing about the connections it already handed over, and the old
restart path went through `stop()`, which dropped them and their shelf
subscriptions.

Verified after the change, in a Release build:

    TCP 127.0.0.1:9020 (LISTEN)
    TCP [::1]:9020     (LISTEN)
    LAN address → refused;  127.0.0.1 and ::1 → connect

7 tests cover the peer check, including the two cases a naive version gets
wrong: an IPv4-mapped loopback peer (`::ffff:127.0.0.1`) is local and must be
served, and a hostname merely containing "localhost" must not be.

perf(bluetooth): stop running system_profiler and pmset on the main thread

Refreshing Bluetooth battery levels shelled out to `system_profiler` and
`pmset` synchronously, from the main thread, at launch and again on every
connect, disconnect and refresh. Measured here: `system_profiler
SPBluetoothDataType -json` takes ~200 ms, `pmset -g accps` ~15 ms, and the
refresh ran four times in the first twenty seconds of a session — most of a
second of main-thread stalls for two numbers that nothing was waiting on.

The refresh is now in two halves. The IORegistry and the preference files are
read in-process in well under a millisecond and still publish synchronously;
the two subprocesses run on a utility queue and republish when they answer.
Their last answers are kept, so the cheap pass never briefly forgets a level
it already knew.

Separately, the `system_profiler` reading is now shared for 30 seconds. It was
being taken once for battery levels and again, per device, for the
vendor/product lookup that identifies the model — so a single connect spawned
it at least twice. Connect and disconnect drop the cached reading, which is
exactly when it stops describing reality and exactly when something is about
to ask.

Verified by running the Release binary in the foreground and comparing its
output before and after, with AirPods Pro connected: same device found, same
model detected, same 21% battery, listening-mode changes still observed —
with the subprocess passes down from four to two, and neither of them on the
main thread.

One visible consequence, and it is the right trade: on a cold start the
battery percentage can arrive a moment after the device does. The connect HUD
already waits briefly for a level before showing, and the existing pmset
fallback fires in that window, which is what the "missing battery after
refresh" line in the log is.

No unit tests: this is queue placement and a cache in a manager with no pure
logic to extract, and the evidence that matters is the before/after run above.

removed mid-drag would be resurrected by the next update.

the cells are covered by `DraggableClickView`, a real NSView that swallows mouse
events, where a SwiftUI gesture would never fire. Drawing the band in `draw(_:)`

fix(shelf): drag files out as real file URLs, not plain text

`createPasteboardItem` waited 5s on a semaphore that always deadlocked (see the
earlier commit), then fell through to writing `item.displayName` as plain text.
That is why dropping onto Finder or Mail produced text instead of the file.

Hand AppKit the `NSURL` instead of hand-rolling an `NSPasteboardItem`: it
declares `public.file-url`, `public.url`, `public.url-name` and the legacy
filenames binding in one go, which is what Finder, Mail attachments and Slack
uploads actually look for. An item whose URL can't be resolved is now dropped
from the drag rather than degraded to text.

Second, independent cause of broken drag-out: dragging out necessarily takes the
cursor off the notch, so the hover-exit timer closed the panel mid-drag and tore
down the NSView acting as the drag source. Gate auto-close on `isDragging`, and
re-evaluate hover once the session ends.

Dragging out also offered `.move` to external apps. AppKit has no way to say
"move is allowed but prefer copy" — the destination decides — and Finder moves
by default when the target is on the same volume, silently relocating the user's
original. Copy is now the default, with moving behind a new `allowMoveOnDrag`
setting.

Drops the security-scope calls on the drag path: since the macOS 26 fix,
`Bookmark` produces plain bookmarks, so `startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()`
always returned false and the paired teardown loop never had anything to do.

fix(bluetooth): stop the device scan re-entering BluetoothAudioManager's own init

Atoll could trap on launch with
`BUG IN CLIENT OF LIBDISPATCH: trying to lock recursively`, but only while a
Bluetooth audio device was connected — which is why it looked intermittent.

The chain, from the crash report:

    applicationDidFinishLaunching
      LockScreenWeatherManager.shared            (once #1)
        observeAccessoryChanges()
          BluetoothAudioManager.shared           (once #2 begins)
            checkInitialDevices()
              refreshBatteryLevelsForConnectedDevices()
                collectSystemProfilerBatteryLevels()
                  systemProfilerBluetoothDictionary()
                    Process.waitUntilExit()  ->  __CFRunLoopRun
                      SwiftUI NSRunLoop.flushObservers
                        ContentView.body -> NotchLayout()
                          InlineHUD default argument 18
                            BluetoothAudioManager.shared   (once #2 AGAIN) -> trap

`Process.waitUntilExit()` on the main thread runs the run loop while it waits.
That hands control to SwiftUI's run-loop observer mid-initialiser, and the body
it evaluates reads `BluetoothAudioManager.shared` because that is a default
argument of `InlineHUD.init` — re-entering the `swift_once` that is still
constructing the instance. A connected audio device is what makes the
`system_profiler` call slow enough for the observer to get a turn.

Deferring the scan to the next main-queue turn lets `shared` finish publishing
first, so the re-entry is impossible by construction. Observer registration and
the 30-second watchdog timer stay in the initialiser; neither spins the run
loop.

Verified against the branch where it reproduced deterministically (4 of 4 runs
trapped before, 112 of 112 tests pass after, twice, with the same Bluetooth
headset still connected).

Worth a separate look: `Process.waitUntilExit()` is called on the main thread in
three places in this file. Deferring the scan removes the re-entrancy, but those
calls still block the main thread while shelling out.

fix(extensions): the RPC port was open to the local network

`ExtensionRPCServer` is documented as listening on localhost, and it was not:
`NWListener(using:on:)` binds the wildcard address, and nothing checked where
a connection came from. Measured on this Mac before the change:

    Atoll  36966  4u  IPv6  TCP *:9020 (LISTEN)
    $ nc -z 192.168.1.105 9020 → succeeded

So any machine on the same Wi-Fi could open the extension API — where a client
declares who it is by putting a `bundleIdentifier` in the request — and drive
the shelf, live activities, lock-screen widgets and notch experiences.

Now bound to the loopback address of each family. Two listeners rather than
one because a socket bound to 127.0.0.1 does not accept ::1 and vice versa,
and a client resolving "localhost" may arrive on either; each is optional, so
a Mac with one family disabled still serves on the other. Every accepted
connection's peer is checked as well — a bind is one line away from being
widened by accident, and the check costs nothing.

Two details worth keeping:

`requiredLocalEndpoint` and `on: port` may not both be given. Passing both
throws EINVAL at init, which is how the first attempt at this fix managed to
bind nothing at all: the listener silently never started, because the error
path logs at a level that is off by default.

A restarted listener no longer tears down live client connections. A listener
failing says nothing about the connections it already handed over, and the old
restart path went through `stop()`, which dropped them and their shelf
subscriptions.

Verified after the change, in a Release build:

    TCP 127.0.0.1:9020 (LISTEN)
    TCP [::1]:9020     (LISTEN)
    LAN address → refused;  127.0.0.1 and ::1 → connect

7 tests cover the peer check, including the two cases a naive version gets
wrong: an IPv4-mapped loopback peer (`::ffff:127.0.0.1`) is local and must be
served, and a hostname merely containing "localhost" must not be.

perf(bluetooth): stop running system_profiler and pmset on the main thread

Refreshing Bluetooth battery levels shelled out to `system_profiler` and
`pmset` synchronously, from the main thread, at launch and again on every
connect, disconnect and refresh. Measured here: `system_profiler
SPBluetoothDataType -json` takes ~200 ms, `pmset -g accps` ~15 ms, and the
refresh ran four times in the first twenty seconds of a session — most of a
second of main-thread stalls for two numbers that nothing was waiting on.

The refresh is now in two halves. The IORegistry and the preference files are
read in-process in well under a millisecond and still publish synchronously;
the two subprocesses run on a utility queue and republish when they answer.
Their last answers are kept, so the cheap pass never briefly forgets a level
it already knew.

Separately, the `system_profiler` reading is now shared for 30 seconds. It was
being taken once for battery levels and again, per device, for the
vendor/product lookup that identifies the model — so a single connect spawned
it at least twice. Connect and disconnect drop the cached reading, which is
exactly when it stops describing reality and exactly when something is about
to ask.

Verified by running the Release binary in the foreground and comparing its
output before and after, with AirPods Pro connected: same device found, same
model detected, same 21% battery, listening-mode changes still observed —
with the subprocess passes down from four to two, and neither of them on the
main thread.

One visible consequence, and it is the right trade: on a cold start the
battery percentage can arrive a moment after the device does. The connect HUD
already waits briefly for a level before showing, and the existing pmset
fallback fires in that window, which is what the "missing battery after
refresh" line in the log is.

No unit tests: this is queue placement and a cache in a manager with no pure
logic to extract, and the evidence that matters is the before/after run above.

Fix hover-to-open dying while the idle face animation is enabled

The closed-notch view chain in ContentView contained a duplicated `else if`
whose body was empty:

    } else if !coordinator.expandingView.show && ... && Defaults[.showNotHumanFace] && !vm.hideOnClosed {
    } else if !isCurrentScreenExpansionVisible && ... && Defaults[.showNotHumanFace] && !vm.hideOnClosed {
        DynamicIslandFaceAnimation()

`isCurrentScreenExpansionVisible` is defined as `coordinator.expandingView.show
&& ...`, so `!coordinator.expandingView.show` strictly implies
`!isCurrentScreenExpansionVisible`. The empty branch is therefore a subset of
the branch below it and always wins whenever nothing is expanding, which is the
normal idle case.

Two consequences:

1. DynamicIslandFaceAnimation() was unreachable in normal use, so the idle
   animation never rendered at all.

2. NotchLayout() has no intrinsic size - `.frame(alignment: .top)` sets no
   width or height, so the notch is sized entirely by its content, and
   `.contentShape(resolvedClipShape)` / `.onHover` derive their hit area from
   that frame. Every other branch renders an explicitly sized rectangle to hold
   the frame open (the fallback `else` uses
   `Rectangle().fill(.clear).frame(width: vm.closedNotchSize.width - 20, ...)`,
   and DynamicIslandFaceAnimation() does the same). Yielding EmptyView collapsed
   the notch to its padding, so `.onHover` stopped firing and hover-to-open
   silently died whenever showNotHumanFace was on and no media was playing.

This is why hover appeared to work only while music was playing: the
MusicLiveActivity branch above supplied the content that kept the frame, and the
hit area, alive.

Removing the dead branch restores both. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged - when
an expansion is visible on the current screen, neither branch matched before and
neither matches now.

Animate the skip glyph like Apple instead of sliding the button

Pressing next/previous track moved the whole button sideways, which is
not what Apple does. `forward.fill` / `backward.fill` are a pair of
triangles, and Apple marches those triangles in the direction of travel
while the button itself stays put.

SkipTrackGlyph draws the glyph as a three-triangle conveyor: the leading
triangle slides out one step and fades, the trailing one takes its
place, and a spare fades in behind it from off-glyph. The end state is
identical to the rest state, so the phase resets without animating and a
fast double-skip fires cleanly each time rather than fighting a
half-finished animation.

Triangle size (0.88x) and spacing (0.52x) were tuned by rendering the
glyph beside `forward.fill` at the same point size, so the resting shape
is indistinguishable from the symbol it replaces.

PanelControlButton takes an optional skipDirection to opt into it; the
old .nudge interaction and its skipNudge plumbing are gone. The +/-10s
seek buttons keep their rotation wiggle, which already matches Apple.

Make every skip press animate, however fast they arrive

Two related defects in advance(). Setting phase = 1 while an animation
was already in flight restated a value the model had already reached, so
SwiftUI saw no change and ran no animation — a second press inside the
0.26s travel was silently swallowed. (The commit that added this claimed
the opposite; that was wrong.) And withAnimation's completion runs when
an animation is interrupted, not only when it finishes, so a stale
completion could snap phase back to 0 underneath a newer run.

Let phase increase monotonically instead — one whole step per press,
never reset — and derive the cycle position from its fractional part.
Because the end of a cycle is pixel-identical to its start, running past
1 is seamless: phase += 1 always changes the model value, so no press is
swallowed, and the completion handler goes away entirely rather than
needing a generation token to police it. Mashing the button now chains
into continuous motion.

Rest state, travel duration and easing curve are unchanged. Verified the
derived geometry: rest state identical at phase 0/1/2/17, five closely
spaced presses target 1..5, cycle N mirrors cycle 0, and state is still
exact after 100000 presses.

With the notch open, a volume change swaps the playback controls for the

nothing animated the fill: the keys deliver discrete 1/16 steps and the

updates are already excluded by the hudDragging guard, so the fill never
fights the cursor, and the forced sync when the row appears still adopts

Animate the skip glyph through an Animatable view

The previous commit stopped the glyph animating at all, on both the lock
screen and the notch. Deriving the cycle position from a wrapping counter
cannot animate: SwiftUI interpolates the rendered values, and because a
whole step lands the triangles exactly where the previous pair sat, the
frames before and after the change are identical — no delta, no motion.
The numeric check in that commit asserted precisely this ("rest state
identical at phase 0/1/2/17") and it was read as a pass.

Move the interpolation onto the phase itself: SkipArrows conforms to
Animatable with phase as its animatableData, so SwiftUI re-evaluates the
body per frame with intermediate values and the derived cycle position
sweeps properly.

Keeping the accumulated phase means a press landing mid-flight extends
the target rather than restating a value the model has already reached
(which SwiftUI treats as no change, swallowing the press), so closely
spaced presses chain into continuous motion. There is no completion
handler, so an interrupted animation has no reset to clobber.

Rest state, travel duration and easing curve are unchanged.

Redesign the clipboard panel

The panel had accumulated the look of a first draft: three stacked
header bars (title, tabs, search) eating the top of a 320x400 window, a
filled-blue tab, and rows whose only structure was a blue type glyph in
a 20pt column above secondary-grey metadata. Every row carried a red
heart, a green copy and a red trash button, so four saturated hues
competed for attention on content that is itself the point.

Rework it around the content:

- Search takes the top row and carries the window's identity, so the
  separate title bar goes; the segmented tabs move onto one line with
  the clear button. Two header rows instead of three.
- The tab selection is a single shape that slides between segments
  rather than a blue rectangle blinking in and out.
- Rows become cards: a 34pt tinted badge holds the type glyph, with the
  preview and a "type · time ago" meta line beside it. Image items show
  an actual thumbnail in the badge instead of a generic glyph.
- Type tints are muted and used consistently in the badge and the meta

fix: fall back to the SF Symbol when the 3D HUD movie cannot be decoded

The 3D Bluetooth HUD icon and its preview tile in Settings play a
bundled looping .mov. Both call sites already have an SF Symbol fallback
for a missing movie, but they decide by asking whether the bundle
contains a file of that name.

That check passes for a file that exists and cannot be played. The
movies are tracked with Git LFS, so a clone made without git-lfs
installed leaves 131-byte pointer stubs carrying the right names and
extensions. Bundle.main.url(forResource:) resolves them, the fallback
never fires, and AVPlayerLayer is handed an undecodable item: the
Settings tile renders as an empty box, and with "3D" selected the HUD
icon area renders blank.

Resolve the URL through inlineHUDAnimationURL, which returns nil unless
the file's header sniffs as a real QuickTime/MP4 container, so both call
sites degrade to the symbol they already know how to draw.

This does not affect release builds, which ship the real assets; it
affects contributors who clone without git-lfs. The proper cure there is
`git lfs install && git lfs pull`, after which the same code path picks
the movies up again with no further changes.

Validate each bundle candidate, and the atom size as well as its type

Two review findings on the sniff, both correct.

The candidates were coalesced with ?? before validation, which selects
on existence alone: a stub in the BluetoothHUDAnimations subdirectory
would have masked a real movie at the bundle root and returned nil.
Validate each candidate in turn and take the first playable one. (Not
reachable with the current bundle layout, where the movies are flattened
to the resources root so only one candidate ever resolves — but the
lookup exists precisely because the layout is not guaranteed.)

The sniff also read only the atom type at bytes 4-7 and ignored the size
at 0-3, so a truncated or malformed file carrying four plausible
characters at offset 4 passed and reached the player, which is the exact
failure this guard exists to prevent. Parse the first atom by the
QuickTime/ISO BMFF rules: size 0 runs to EOF, size 1 takes a 64-bit
extended size, 2...7 cannot hold its own header, and anything else must
fit inside the file.

Also switches to the failable String(bytes:encoding:) initialiser that
SwiftLint's optional_data_string_conversion rule asks for.

Verified against the eight real assets (all accepted) and crafted files:
an LFS pointer, a truncated ftyp, an impossible size-4 atom, a size-0
atom, a 64-bit size beyond EOF, an unknown atom type, and a missing
file — all classified correctly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Require a structurally complete movie, not just a plausible first atom

Checking one header accepted a file consisting solely of
`00 00 00 08 ftyp`: the declared extent matched the file length, so it
passed while containing no metadata and no media.

Walk the top-level atom chain instead. It must tile the file exactly and
include a `moov`, which is where the playable metadata lives — in these
assets it is the last atom, after a 340 KB `mdat`, so the walk reaches
EOF by necessity.

Only the *first* atom is matched against the known leading types. That
is what separates a movie from a text file such as an un-fetched LFS
pointer, and it is all that should be constrained: a valid container may
carry any number of unfamiliar top-level atoms, and rejecting one would
silently disable a working animation — a worse failure than the
malformed-file case this guards. Subsequent atoms need only a printable
four-character type and an extent that fits inside the file. The walk is
bounded so a malformed chain cannot spin.

Verified against the eight real assets and eleven crafted files: the
reported ftyp-only case, an LFS pointer, ftyp+mdat with no moov, a moov
running past EOF, trailing slack after the last atom, an impossible
size-4 atom, an unknown leading type, a missing file, a moov with size 0,
a complete minimal movie, and a valid file carrying an exotic `uuid`
atom mid-chain — which must still be accepted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Avoid trapping on an atom extent near UInt64.max

`offset + extent <= fileSize` evaluates the sum before the bound, and
`extent` is read straight out of the file: an extended-size atom
declaring UInt64.max overflows the addition, which traps. Confirmed by
isolating the expression against a crafted 24-byte file — an 8-byte
`ftyp` followed by an extended-size `mdat` declaring UInt64.max — which
crashed with exit 133.

That is strictly worse than the empty frame this validator exists to
prevent: a malformed asset would take the app down rather than fall back
to the SF Symbol.

Compare by subtraction instead. The loop condition keeps
`offset <= fileSize`, so `fileSize - offset` cannot underflow; the
invariant is now load-bearing and noted at the guard.

Adds the requested regression cases: an extended-size atom declaring
UInt64.max both before and after a valid `moov`, each rejected without
trapping. Twenty-one cases pass, including the eight real assets.

Add a setting for whether clipboard history is saved to disk

Closes the gap reported in #727. "Enable Clipboard Manager" stops the
polling timer, but history already captured stays in UserDefaults as
plain JSON indefinitely, and there is no way to use the clipboard
manager without writing what you copy to disk. For the passwords, OTPs
and API keys the issue is concerned with, stopping future capture is
only half the ask.

"Save History Across Restarts" (Privacy section, on by default so
existing installs are unchanged) makes history session-only when off:
nothing is written, what is already stored is erased, and nothing is
read back at launch.

Erasing on the way out matters as much as not writing. Turning the
setting off purges the stored blob immediately, and a launch-time purge
runs before anything can read it back. That purge deliberately does not
go through the manager: the singleton is created lazily — often not
until the user first opens the clipboard, sometimes never — so leaving
it to `init` would let history the user asked not to keep sit on disk
for the whole session.

Pinned items are untouched either way; they are an explicit choice to
keep something, and a history setting should not silently discard them.

Verified against the running app: with the setting on, a copy is written
and survives a quit; with it off, new copies are never written and a
blob seeded by a previous session is gone after launch without opening
the clipboard UI at all.

Refs: https://github.com/Ebullioscopic/Atoll/issues/727

Keep retrying the media key tap until Accessibility is granted

CGEvent.tapCreate fails outright without Accessibility, and granting it
does not relaunch the app — so the single attempt in start() left the tap
uninstalled for the rest of the session. The media keys then reach macOS
untouched: the native HUD draws, and brightness gets no HUD at all,
because brightness is only detected when this app drives the change
(volume has a CoreAudio observer to fall back on, which is why only
brightness looked broken).

The reported workaround — switch control animation to another style and
back — worked by accident: that restarts the observer, which calls
start() again, which retries the tap.

start() now installs the tap through installTap() and, on failure, polls
for it: every 2s for the first minute, then every 15s, giving up after an
hour. AXIsProcessTrusted() gates each attempt so a failing tap creation
is not paid for on every tick. A tap installed this late has missed every
key so far, so it re-suppresses the native HUD on the way in.

MediaKeyTapRetryPolicy holds the schedule so it can be tested without a
permission prompt.

Closes #601

never appears. The Live Activities copies of these controls were already

Stop inline lyrics crowding the notch transport controls

With the calendar shown, shouldShowSideLyrics is false and lyrics render as
a third line inside songInfo instead of in the side panel — and unlike the
side-panel path, nothing gives the layout more room for it:
sideLyricsRequiredNotchWidth() returns 0 when showCalendar is set, and the
open notch height is a constant.

The player column was:

    VStack { songInfoAndSlider; playbackControls }

where songInfoAndSlider is a GeometryReader. A GeometryReader accepts
whatever size it is offered rather than sizing to its content, so it filled
the column and the visible gap above the controls was simply the part it
had not drawn into. Adding a line pushed the content down into that gap,
which is why the elapsed-time row ended up against the buttons while the
buttons themselves never moved.

The reader was only there to hand a width to the marquee labels. Measure
that in a background overlay through a preference key instead, let the
stack size to its content, and separate the two with
Spacer(minLength: MusicPlayerLayout.minimumControlsGap). Spacer still
absorbs the slack when there is room, so the two-line layout is unchanged.

Measured on a captured notch, distance from the elapsed-time row to the
transport row: lyrics off 97px before and after; lyrics on 45px before,
102px after.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Revert "Stop inline lyrics crowding the notch transport controls"

This reverts commit 8af3c3d8e32ba957e78ecedaa46367c81759f6f9.

fix: give the notch room for the inline lyrics line

The home player lays its text and slider out inside a greedy GeometryReader,
so the gap above the transport controls is simply that reader's leftover
space. Turning inline lyrics on adds a third text line, which takes its
height straight out of that gap and leaves the controls crowded against the
slider.

Grow the open notch by one lyrics line whenever the home tab is rendering
inline lyrics, following the existing per-view sizing adjustments. The extra
height is applied while inline lyrics are enabled rather than only while a
line is on screen, so the notch height stays stable between lyric lines
instead of jumping as lines come and go.

fix: stop short text from scrolling in the marquee

MarqueeText renders two copies of the text separated by a 20pt gap and
recovers the width of one copy by halving the measured loop. The gap was
never subtracted, so every string measured 10pt wider than it really is and
any text landing within 10pt of its column was mistaken for text that
overflows -- which is why a short artist name scrolls while the song title,
which measures itself with NSString.size(withAttributes:), does not. The
same overstated width also made each scroll cycle travel 10pt too far.

Subtract the gap before halving, name the spacing constant that all three
call sites were repeating, and pull the arithmetic out into a testable
static so the off-by-a-gap cannot come back unnoticed.

fix: untangle the lyrics and calendar toggles

"Show lyrics on the side (requires calendar off)" and "Show calendar" each
disabled the other, so once both were on neither could be turned back off.
The notch has its own lyrics quick-toggle that does not consult the calendar
setting, so reaching that state and getting stuck took two clicks.

The exclusion also misdescribes the feature. enableLyrics is the general
lyrics switch, not a side-panel switch: NotchHomeView renders lyrics inline
under the artist name when the calendar is on, and gives them their own side
panel when it is off. Both combinations are supported and one of them was
unreachable from Settings.

Drop the mutual exclusion, rename the toggle back to "Show lyrics", and
replace the "requires calendar off" wording with a caption that says which
of the two presentations the current settings produce. The genuine gates --
Minimalistic UI and Dynamic Island media controls -- are left in place, and
the side-panel width and offset sliders still appear only when the panel is
the active presentation.

Introduced in #741.

docs: say what actually controls where lyrics appear

The caption under "Show lyrics" named the current presentation but not the
setting that decides it, which leaves the reader knowing lyrics moved
without knowing why or how to move them back. Say which setting is the
lever, on both the lyrics and the calendar side.

fix: stop synced lyrics from running ahead of the music

The Now Playing adapter reports the playback position together with the
instant it was sampled, and estimated position is computed from that pair.
Atoll ran the adapter without --micros, so the anchor arrived as an ISO-8601
string formatted yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss'Z' -- whole seconds. The reported
position keeps its milliseconds, so truncating only the anchor biases every
estimate forward by the discarded fraction: a sampled reading anchored at
1787320813.448212 came through as ...813.000000, putting the estimate 448ms
ahead, and the error rerolls with each update.

Stream with --micros and read timestampEpochMicros, elapsedTimeMicros and
durationMicros, falling back to the string form for adapters that ignore the
flag.

Also fix a second way the pair came apart: a diff update carrying a new
elapsed time but no timestamp kept the *previous* anchor, so the estimate ran
ahead by the age of that anchor. Position and anchor are now adopted or
carried forward together.

The LRC parser had its own timing bugs, all of which survive into what is
displayed:

- Three-digit millisecond timestamps failed the pattern outright. The
  optional fraction accepted one or two digits and the closing bracket then
  did not match, so those lines were dropped silently.
- A single-digit fraction was read as hundredths, making ".5" 50ms instead
  of 500ms.
- Only the first timestamp on a line was used. LRC writes a repeated chorus
  once with one tag per repetition, so every repeat after the first lost its
  timing -- and the unconsumed tags were rendered as part of the lyric text.
- The [offset:] tag, which exists precisely to correct timing, was ignored.

Move the parser into LRCParser so it can be tested, and cover each of the
above.

Finally, replace the fixed 300ms sync poll with a sleep until the next
line's own timestamp, bounded to stay responsive to seeks. Polling on a
fixed interval shows every line up to one interval late no matter how
accurate the clock underneath is.

fix: leave minimalistic UI out of the inline lyrics height

The minimalistic player draws lyrics whenever they are enabled, without
consulting the calendar, and already resizes for them through its own
publisher. Applying the inline lyrics adjustment there reserved room for a
line the standard player is not drawing, and made the calculated height
depend on showCalendar in a mode whose resize path does not observe it -- so
toggling the calendar left notchSize stale until some other event resized
the notch.

Restrict the adjustment to the standard player. Also add the CHANGELOG
entries, which went missing when the first attempt at this fix was reverted.

fix: address review findings on the settings scope pass

- Read the temperature preference with UnitTemperature(forLocale:) instead of
  inferring it from a formatted measurement. The Temperature control in
  Language & Region is set independently of the measurement system, and the
  formatter follows the measurement system: a US-region Mac set to Celsius
  reported Fahrenheit, and a metric Mac set to Fahrenheit reported Celsius.
  Both were verified against the running system.

- Name the real setting in the volume-key help text. It referred to "Route
  volume from the external app"; the toggle is called "Enable external volume
  control listener", so nobody could find it.

- Reindex the widget layout picker in settings search. It was still listed as
  "Layout" with the matching highlight ID, so the search result could not
  scroll to the renamed picker.

- Apply the reminder live activity prerequisite to every reminder control.
  The alignment picker and vertical offset slider stayed enabled when the
  live activity was off but the widget toggle had been left on, and the
  Calendar tab's copy of the widget toggle had no prerequisite at all.

fix: show the empty state when the AirPlay picker has no devices

shouldShowAirPlay required a non-empty device list, but
shouldShowRouteSelector stands down whenever merged output is on. With
merged output active, the picker open, and nothing discovered, both branches
were false and the panel rendered nothing -- so airPlaySection's own "No
AirPlay outputs available" message could never appear.

The merged mode owns the slot outright, so the emptiness check belongs to the
section, which already handles it.

docs: note that the inline lyrics height applies to the standard player

The entry described the sizing rule without its exclusion, so it read as
covering Minimalistic UI too.

fix: gate step sizes on who actually owns the keys

SystemHUDManager.resolvedControlFlags() hands volume and brightness to the
external provider only while DDC integration is enabled *and* the selected
provider is running. Settings gated the step-size controls on the settings
alone, so quitting BetterDisplay or Lunar left them greyed out even though
Atoll had resumed handling the keys and the saved step sizes were in effect
again.

The volume controls were gated on enableExternalVolumeControlListener by
itself, which does not even imply the integration is on -- so the volume
steps could be disabled while Atoll owned volume outright.

Derive externalOwnsVolume and externalOwnsBrightness from the same condition
the manager uses and gate all four steppers and both captions on them. The
view already observes BetterDisplayManager and LunarManager, whose isRunning
is published, so the controls re-enable as soon as the provider exits.

docs: correct the changelog for the two follow-up fixes

The temperature entry still described the MeasurementFormatter approach that
was replaced, and the step-size entry described only the wording change, not
the gating fix that followed it.

feat: sweep the lyrics highlight in time with the music

The current line was lit by a fixed left-to-right gradient, so the whole line
changed colour the instant it became current and then sat still. Drive the
gradient from playback position instead: MusicManager exposes the time window
the current line occupies and how far through it playback has moved, and the
panel redraws on a TimelineView so the boundary between sung and unsung
travels along the line as it is sung. The two stops either side of the
playhead keep that boundary a soft edge rather than a hard wipe.

Show instrumental breaks as music notes rather than as nothing. LRC marks
where singing stops with a bare timestamp, so the gap is delimited by the
lyrics themselves and needs no heuristic -- but the parser was discarding
those markers as empty lines, which lost the gap and also left the inline
lyric holding the last sung line through the whole break. Keep them, and
render a run of five seconds or more as notes, so breaths between lines do
not flicker. A long intro before the first line is marked the same way.

fix: sweep the whole row, mark breaks inline, honour a cleared position

Three fixes to the lyrics highlight and one to the payload decoding.

The music notes never swept. The gradient was handed to foregroundStyle on
the HStack holding them, and a gradient used as a foreground style is
resolved against each leaf view's own bounds -- so all three glyphs got the
whole gradient repeated inside them and nothing appeared to move. Overlay the
gradient and mask it to the row instead, which stretches one gradient across
the whole thing. Sung lines go through the same path so both behave alike.

The intro marker never swept either, for a different reason: it is keyed to
index -1, the index the current line holds before the first line starts, and
lyricWindow(at:) rejected anything below zero, so progress was pinned at 0
for the entire intro. Give -1 the window it describes, from the start of the
track to the first line.

Instrumental breaks were invisible in the inline lyric shown beside the
calendar. That view renders only when the line is non-empty, and preserving
the gap markers made the line empty for the length of a break -- so the row
silently vanished. Show the notes there too, driven by the same
isInstrumentalBreak test the panel uses, now on MusicManager so there is one
definition of what counts as a break.

Finally, distinguish an omitted position from one explicitly set to null when
decoding an adapter update. A diff omits what has not changed, so an absent
position means "carry the last one forward", while a null position is the
sender saying it no longer has one. Optional decoding renders both as nil, so
a cleared position was mistaken for an unchanged one and the stale pair kept
being extrapolated from. Only the null case changes behaviour; omitted is
handled exactly as before.

fix: rebuild lyric rows when the duration arrives

Duration closes the last line's window, so a trailing outro is only marked
once it is known. Rows were rebuilt on the lyrics changing alone, and the
duration can land after them.

fix: make the output picker's volume slider usable

Two faults, both of which end with the popover disappearing the moment it is
clicked.

Changing the volume from the picker raised the notch's own volume HUD.
HUDSuppressionCoordinator exists for exactly this and SystemChangesObserver
honours it, but only BluetoothAudioManager ever called it -- so Atoll's own
volume controls did not suppress Atoll's own HUD. The HUD then put a second
slider on screen and swapped out the content the popover was anchored to,
which tore the popover down mid-drag. Suppress the HUD from
MediaOutputVolumeViewModel, refreshed on every change so a drag holds it off
until shortly after the last movement. This covers the lock screen panel's
slider too, which uses the same model.

The picker also gave up the notch as soon as the pointer was not over it.
isMediaOutputPopoverActive was presentation AND hover, but a popover is its
own window, so moving into it reads as leaving the notch -- and any moment
before the popover reported the pointer let the auto-close timer shut the
notch and take the popover with it. Presentation alone is what the stats,
timer and clipboard popovers already use. The hover tracking is now unused
and is removed rather than left write-only.

fix: clear the lyric when no line is current

updateCurrentLyric only wrote currentLyrics when it had a line to write. When
playback moved before the first line -- a fresh track, or a seek back into the
intro -- the index dropped to -1 but the text was left alone, so the previous
line stayed on screen as though it were being sung.

Clear it, and drive the inline instrumental marker off isInInstrumentalBreak
rather than off the line being blank. There is no current line during an intro
to blank out, so testing the text missed the case entirely and the compact
view showed a stale lyric where the notes belonged. The marquee is suppressed
for the length of the break.

fix: settle the lyric text independently of the index

Two paths still put a lyric on screen before it was sung.

updateCurrentLyric wrote the text only when the index moved, but lyrics are
applied with the index already at -1, so a fresh set left whatever text was
there standing. Settle the text from the index every pass instead, comparing
before assigning so the sync tick does not republish an unchanged value.

applyLyricsToDisplay then filled the intro in with the first line outright.
That predates the sweep and was defensible when the line was static, but a
highlight travelling across a line that is not being sung reads as broken --
and an intro long enough to notice now shows the instrumental marker, which
is what is actually happening. Drop the fallback.

Also scroll to rows by asking the row list rather than bounds-checking against
syncedLyrics. The intro marker is keyed to -1, which a lower bound of zero
rejects, so it could become current while staying off-screen.

fix: let the output pickers share their open flag without clobbering

Four views can present an output picker -- media output and AirPlay, in both
the standard and minimalistic players -- and each assigned
vm.isMediaOutputPopoverActive directly. They share one flag, so whichever ran
last won: closing one picker wrote false while another was still open, and
the notch auto-closed underneath it. Each onDisappear cleared it outright for
the same reason.

Presenters now register against a token that is stable for the life of the
view, and the flag follows whether any of them is still open. It is
private(set), so a direct assignment no longer compiles.

Pre-existing -- the old presentation-AND-hover expression had the same race --
but worth fixing here since this PR is what makes presentation the thing that
holds the notch open.

fix: mark the intro, and keep lyrics moving without a duration

Two ways the intro marker failed to appear.

rows(for:duration:) decided the intro marker from "nothing added yet". If the
first parsed entry was itself a qualifying gap marker it claimed the first
row, so the test never fired and the intro had no row -- while
currentLyricIndex sat at -1 through it, leaving nothing highlighted and no
scroll target. Decide it from the first timestamp instead.

estimatedPlaybackPosition clamps to songDuration, which is zero until the
duration arrives and for streams that never report one, so it answered zero
however far playback had actually got. The lyric sync loop then pinned the
current line at -1 and the sweep at zero for the whole track.
applyLyricsToDisplay already worked around this with max(..., elapsedTime);
that fallback is now a named helper used by all three callers, so the next one
does not have to remember.

fix: close the seam above the lock screen notch, and use Apple's lock

A sliver of wallpaper showed between the notch and the top of the screen.
safeAreaInsets.top is fractional on notched hardware -- 33.5pt on a 14-inch --
and AppKit rounds a window's frame to whole points while SwiftUI lays the
content out at whatever size it was handed. Asking for a 33.5pt window gave a
34pt one holding 33.5pt of content, and since the content view is anchored at
the bottom-left, the leftover half point sat along the top edge. Round the
notch to whole points, and size the content view from the window's actual
frame rather than the frame that was requested.

Use the system lock symbol instead of the bundled Lottie. The drawn one is
much lighter in the stroke and reads as a different icon next to everything
else macOS puts on the lock screen. A symbol .replace transition gives the
open-to-closed change the shackle movement the animation was there for.

Also settle the music panel's default width, which the app disagreed with
itself about: the stored default was 350 while "reset to default" set 420 --
which was also the slider's maximum, so resetting pinned it at the top of its
range. Both now come from one constant at 390, a little wider than the old
starting width, and the slider reaches 460 so there is still room to widen.

feat: sweep the lock screen lyrics too

The lock screen player drew the current line flat and showed nothing at all
through an instrumental break, while the notch had both the sweep and the
markers. Give it the same treatment.

The sweep lived as private helpers on the side panel, so it moves to
LyricSweep: the gradient, a modifier that overlays and masks it across a whole
row, and the three notes. Both the notch and the lock screen use it, which is
also why the notch's own copies could not simply be shared -- they were
written against that one view's colours.

fix: give play/pause its size back on the lock screen

Sizing the secondary controls to match Apple grew their frame from 32 to 40
collapsed (56 to 62 expanded) and left play/pause at 54/80. The gap between
them closed from 1.7x to 1.35x, so the row read as five buttons of the same
size rather than a primary control with four around it.

Raise play/pause to 58/84 with a 28/39 glyph. The row grows by four points
rather than restoring the old ratio outright, since the panel's height is
fixed and the volume and lyrics rows sit under it. Its glyph now sits
proportionally larger in its highlight than the others, which is what Apple
does with the control you aim at without looking.

fix: bring the lock screen panel back if it goes missing, and settle its look

hidePanel clears the window's content view, so anything that hides the media
panel while the screen is still locked leaves it gone -- nothing brings it
back until the next lock. Rather than chase every route that can hide it,
the lock-state poll that already runs every 500ms now checks that a panel
which should be on screen still is, and re-presents it if not. showPanel
already returns early when the widget is switched off, so this cannot
resurrect a panel that was deliberately disabled.

Also lower the resting position by 16pt, clear of the clock -- the panel
grows upward as the volume and lyrics rows appear, so it needs room above it
-- and thin the volume capsule from 14/16 to 11/13.

fix: tighten the lock screen player's padding and drop it lower

The panel top-aligns its content, so the volume row's reserved height was
showing up as dead space under the capsule: 46/50pt held for a row that
draws a 14pt gap plus a 10/13pt capsule. Trimmed to 32/36 and split the
outer vertical inset so the bottom is 4-6pt tighter than the top, and
pulled the horizontal inset in so the widened panel spends the extra
width on content rather than on margins.

Also thinned the collapsed capsule to 10pt and lowered the resting
position by another 24pt, which clears the login avatar instead of
sitting level with it.

feat: give the expanded lock screen player a lyrics column

Expanded is the mode you open to read along, but it showed the same
single line the collapsed player does, stacked under the controls. It
now puts the whole song in a column beside the player -- scrolling
itself to the line being sung, sweeping that line in time, and marking
instrumental stretches with notes -- and widens the panel by exactly
that column rather than growing taller.

The scrolling swept list and its row model moved out of the notch's
lyrics tab into SyncedLyricsList so both read the same song the same
way; the notch keeps its own colours and metrics through the style.

fix: leave the volume bar grey until you reach for it

Apple only gives the volume bar full colour and full brightness while
you are on it; resting at 0.92 opacity and full saturation made it
compete with the artwork behind it. It now sits desaturated at 0.55 and
comes up to colour on hover and to full strength on drag.

fix: grey the seek bar at rest and let it swell from its middle

Three things about the transport slider, all visible in the lock screen
player. It carried full colour and full brightness at rest, which the

fix: let the expanded player stay open long enough to read

fix: lay the expanded player out around the lyrics column

Adding the column exposed how loosely the expanded side was arranged.

The artwork was a fixed 230pt square in a panel whose height grows as
the volume and output rows appear, so it floated with a band of dead
space above and below it; it now fills the content height, 200-330.

The middle column stacked title, progress and transport with a fixed
20pt between them and centred the clump, leaving a gap above the title
and another under the controls. Title is pinned to the top now,
transport to the bottom, and the slack is taken up between them.

The device row was being cut in half by the panel's bottom edge: the
accessory reserve counted the section's own padding but not the 14pt
the controls stack puts above it.

The lyrics column gained a hairline spine, wider text insets so it
clears the panel's rounded corner, and the visualizer no longer sits
adrift in the corner next to it.

fix: stop the expanded player reserving height it already had

Three separate faults, all showing as gaps.

Lyrics ran off the right edge instead of wrapping. Each row claimed the
full column width and *then* added its own horizontal insets, so every
line was laid out 36pt wider than the column it sat in. Padding now goes
inside the width claim.

The panel was growing by a fixed reserve for the volume row and another
for the output list, on top of a height the middle column already had
room for. The extra went somewhere -- into the two gaps either side of
the progress bar, since the column pinned its title to the top and its
transport to the bottom and split the slack between them. Expanded now
measures what the column needs and grows only by the shortfall, and the
column spaces its three blocks evenly and centres them.

Play/pause read as lagging the click: the glyph swap rode whatever
animation happened to be ambient when isPlaying changed. It is pinned to
a 0.16s snappy now, and the press-release is 0.15s rather than 0.24s.

fix: size the expanded artwork off the width it can actually have

The lyrics kept running past the right edge even after the row insets
were fixed, because the overflow was never the rows -- it was the HStack.
The transport row has a hard minimum width and will not be squeezed, so
when the artwork was sized off the panel's height alone the three columns
asked for more than the panel had, and the surplus came out of whatever
sat furthest right.

Artwork is now the flexible column, taking the smaller of the height it
can fill and the width left after the transport row and the lyrics
column are served -- and the transport minimum is measured from the
slots actually on screen, since that row is user-configurable. Turning
the column on also widens the panel by more than the column itself, so
the player side keeps the width it had.

feat: sweep the lyrics word by word, in reading order

A gradient over a Text sweeps it as one rectangle, so a line that wrapped
lit its second row level with its first instead of after it -- the
highlight ran straight down both at once, which is nothing like being
sung.

The line is laid out as individual words now, wrapped by a small flow
layout, and each word gets its own slice of the line's progress. The
slices come from word length: longer words take longer to sing, near
enough, and counting characters keeps the pace even across a wide glyph.

Still an estimate rather than real per-word timing -- lrclib carries
line-level timestamps only, as the parser notes above. It just estimates
in reading order now.

feat: notice Firefox downloads as well as Chromium ones

Download detection only knew the extensions Chromium and Safari use, so a
Firefox download went unremarked: it writes its bytes to `archive.zip.part`.

The three conventions differ only in the extension -- each is the destination
name with something appended -- so the extension is now one set and the
destination is the temporary name with its extension stripped, rather than a
Chromium-shaped special case with a Firefox path bolted beside it.

That pairing is also what tells a finished download from an abandoned one, in
place of watching for a file that had not been there before. Firefox creates
the destination up front, as an empty placeholder next to the part file, so it
had already been seen by the time the download finished -- a completed Firefox
download would have been read as a cancellation and the live activity yanked
away without its checkmark. A download now counts as finished when the file it
was aiming at holds data, which is true of a Chromium rename and of a Firefox
rename, and false while the placeholder is still empty -- including in the
moment between Firefox deleting a cancelled part file and its placeholder.
